# Introduction

This notebook aims to provide insight into the amount of daily cannabis use in Canada, using a data set covering the period from 1961-2018. The data set is available for download from Statistics Canada  [here.](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3610059701)

# Analysis

## How has the amount of daily cannabis users in Canada changed over time?

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# No scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

# Load and tidy dataset
data <- read.csv("36100597.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  filter(
    age_group != "15 years and over",
    frequency_of_use != "Total, all frequencies"
  ) |>
  select(ref_date,age_group,frequency_of_use,value) |>
  filter(
    frequency_of_use == "Daily"
  ) |>
  drop_na(value)

# Plot daily cannabis users by age group over time
data |>
  filter(frequency_of_use == "Daily") |>
  mutate(age_group = trimws(age_group)) |>
  group_by(ref_date, age_group) |>
  summarize(sum_value = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ref_date, y = sum_value)) +
  geom_line(color = viridis(1)[1], linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ age_group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Cannabis Users by Age Group",
    subtitle = "Canada (1961–2018)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"),
    # Increase margin space on right side
    plot.margin = margin(15, 30, 15, 15)
  )
```

This multi-panel line graph shows daily cannabis users in Canada from 1961-2018, separated by age group. The x-axis represents the year, the y-axis represents the number of daily cannabis users for a given age group.

The 15-17 age group has the lowest number daily users. There is a sharp increase during the 1970s, with numbers peaking near 60,000, with a decline following in the late 1980s to early 1990s. Another small rise occurs in the late 1990s and early 2000s. There is a slight decrease toward 2018.

The 18-24 age group has a higher amount of daily usage than teenagers, with a rapid increase from the 1960s to the late 1970s. A decline followed in the early 1990s, but usage rises again after 2000, ending at the highest point of the series (above 300,000).

The 25-44 age group demonstrates a strong and steady upward trend overall, with gradual growth from the 1960s to the 1980s. This group had the largest number of users by 2018, reaching roughly 450,000.

The 45-64 age group has very low and stable usage before 1990, with a period of rapid growth beginning in the late 1990s (the sharpest increase occurring after 2000). Numbers reach over 300,000 by 2018.

The plot demonstrates that daily cannabis use generally increased over time across all age groups, with older age groups (25-44 and 45-64) showing the most sustained, long-term growth. Younger groups show more fluctuations over time.

# Conclusion

Daily cannabis use increased substantially across all age groups between 1961 and 2018. Adults aged 25-44 eperienced the highest overall number of daily users by the end of the period. The 45-64 age group showed the fastest late-period growth, especially after 2000. Younger age groups (15-17, 18-24) displayed more fluctuations and periods of decline. The overall trend suggests that cannabis use became increasingly common among older adults over time.
